Article Title: The OGs reunite: SAD gets 'bada bhai' tag in Punjab, but BJP has bigger ambitions
Article Text:
BJP, Akalis have reunited for the 2027 Punjab elections, but will nostalgia be enough?

Sukhbir Badal invoked his late father as he announced reunion with the BJP.

The hot and cold relationship of SAD and BJP.

NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws. The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and the Shiromani Akali Dal ( SAD ) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections , reviving a partnership that once governed the state for 15 years across three terms.The reunion, announced on the Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, brings together parties whose relationship was famously described by former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal as "nau-maas da rishta", the bond between the nail and the flesh.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first."Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said in a post on X, adding that the partnership, nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, had "stood the test of time".Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced the reunion alongside BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, called the Akali Dal the NDA's "oldest ally" and said PM Modi had described the development by saying the "NDA is now complete".Shah also said SAD would retain its senior-partner status, adding that the "big brother" would get the chief minister's post. "Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats.Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," the Union minister said at the joint press conference.The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised.The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring, including Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi in August and a shift in SAD's position on the Centre's delimitation proposal. It also brings together two parties whose electoral fortunes have declined sharply since their separation.However, Punjab is no longer the state in which the old alliance enjoyed its strongest run. AAP has emerged as the dominant force, Congress remains a significant contender, and the BJP and SAD have both undergone changes in their support bases and political strategies.The partnership actually predates the BJP. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, shared power with the Akalis in Punjab as far back as 1967 and 1969. The modern alliance, however, was forged in 1996, when SAD's Moga Declaration pivoted from purely Panthic politics to a broader pitch of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat."The partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. It also helped both parties build a political coalition in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab.The alliance won 93 of 117 assembly seats in 1997, with SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. After losing power to Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 and retained power in 2012, winning 67 and 68 seats respectively.But the emergence of AAP, coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, weakened the alliance. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.The final rupture came in September 2020, when SAD walked out of the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws. Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister on September 17, and the Akali Dal formally ended its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP nine days later.The laws were repealed in November 2021, but the political damage endured.The alliance's decline is evident from its electoral record. In 2007, SAD won 48 seats and the BJP 19, taking their combined tally to 67. They improved to 68 seats in 2012, with SAD winning 56 and the BJP 12. But the numbers fell sharply thereafter. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three. By the 2022 assembly elections, the two parties managed just five seats between them, with SAD winning three and the BJP two.In 2022, SAD secured 18.38% of the vote and the BJP 6.60%, while AAP swept the election with 92 seats and a 42.01% vote share.Their separate performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections provided another reason to reconsider the alliance. The BJP failed to win any of Punjab's 13 seats despite securing 18.56% of the vote. SAD won one seat, Bathinda, with 13.42%.Together, their vote shares added up to nearly 32%, compared with 26.30% for Congress and 26.02% for AAP.The numbers make a case for pooling their support bases, although the combined vote share does not automatically translate into transferable votes or assembly seats.For the BJP, the alliance offers access to SAD's traditional rural and Sikh support networks. For the Akali Dal, it brings back a national ally and an opportunity to rebuild its electoral machinery, which is the BJP's strong suit.Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as more than an electoral arrangement."This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.The old partners are back again, but the state the BJP and SAD are returning to is markedly different from the one they left behind in 2020.The 2027 assembly election will be the alliance's first major state-level electoral test without Parkash Singh Badal, the five-time CM who died in April 2023. A towering figure in the Akali Dal, he was also a key bridge between the SAD and the BJP. Though Sukhbir Badal was already leading the party before his father's death, he now has to rebuild the party's standing without his political stature and influence.Another factor the alliance must keep in mind is that the farm issue has not disappeared. The repeal of the three farm laws did not automatically undo the distrust they created. Farmers' demands, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price, remain unresolved, keeping the issue politically alive in an agrarian state like Punjab. The BJP-SAD alliance will have to reckon with that trust deficit, particularly in the rural Malwa belt, which is the largest and most populous region covering major farming districts like Bathinda, Mansa, Sangrur, Patiala, Ludhiana and Muktsar.This is why the choice of Gurpurab for the reunion announcement is rich in symbolism. PM Modi had announced the repeal of the farm laws on the occasion in November 2021. The two parties have now chosen the same religious occasion to announce their political reconciliation. Whether that symbolism can translate into renewed trust among farmers is a different question.Another thing that has changed is that the Akali Dal can no longer assume that it commands the entire Panthic vote. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, independent candidates Amritpal Singh and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won from Khadoor Sahib and Faridkot, respectively. Between them, they also led in 15 assembly segments.This makes the party's return to its traditional Panthic space more difficult. The SAD has tried to reconnect with its core constituency through issues of Sikh identity and historical memory. The controversy surrounding 'Satluj', a film based on activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's work documenting alleged extrajudicial killings in Punjab, offered one such opportunity. After the film was taken down from an OTT platform, Sukhbir Badal announced screenings across the state, saying young people should know about the events it depicts.Six years on its own have transformed the BJP from a junior partner that contested just 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats into a more assertive player. Under the old arrangement, the SAD contested 94 assembly seats and the BJP 23, largely in urban constituencies. For the Lok Sabha elections, the split was 10 seats for the Akalis and three for the BJP.Its vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha election rose to 18.56 per cent, up from 9.63 per cent in 2019. The BJP contested all 13 seats in 2024, compared with just three under the old seat-sharing arrangement in 2019. Though it won no seats, the saffron party's vote share was higher than the SAD's 13.42 per cent. In the 2022 assembly election, the BJP had polled 6.60 per cent and won two seats.The party has also strengthened its ranks through a steady stream of defections. In April 2026, AAP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha led six other MPs into the BJP which included Sandeep Pathak, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta and Swati Maliwal. Six of these seven were Rajya Sabha members from Punjab. The exits dealt a major blow to the AAP's parliamentary strength and brought into the BJP leaders who had been closely associated with the party's Punjab strategy. Chadha and Pathak, in particular, had played key roles in the AAP's political and electoral planning.The BJP has since moved to put these former AAP leaders to work against their old party. Chadha and Harbhajan Singh have been named to its Punjab manifesto committee, while Pathak, Mittal, Sahney and other former AAP MPs have been assigned roles in the party's chargesheet committee, which will prepare its case against the Bhagwant Mann government.Earlier, in March 2024, AAP's then Jalandhar MP Sushil Kumar Rinku and Jalandhar West MLA Sheetal Angural had also joined the BJP. In November 2026, three more AAP legislators, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, crossed over. The BJP has also inducted senior Akali leaders, including Surinder Singh Chauhan and Jaswinderpal Sohal, as well as AAP functionaries from Moga led by spokesperson Navdeep Singh Sangha.The BJP's recruitment drive has not been limited to the AAP and SAD. Its Punjab ranks also include former Congress leaders such as Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Singh Badal, Ravneet Singh Bittu and Preneet Kaur.That changes the terms of the reunion. The BJP returns with a larger vote share, a wider organisational footprint and experienced leaders. The SAD, meanwhile, needs the alliance to recover lost ground and reconnect with rural voters. Amit Shah has announced that the BJP is okay with the junior-partner label in the alliance. It is, however, unlikely that the BJP will settle for the old seat-sharing formula.The immediate target of the alliance is the AAP government, which swept to power in 2022 with 92 seats and 42.01 per cent of the vote. Its vote share fell to 26.02 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when it won three seats, but it remains a formidable player.The SAD-BJP reunion gives the opposition a potentially stronger combination of urban and rural networks. It could also help consolidate voters who want an alternative to the AAP government. The drug problem, in particular, is likely to be a central campaign issue.At his press conference, Amit Shah listed three priorities for a future NDA government: eliminating drugs, eliminating corruption and strengthening nationalist forces. He promised that Punjab would be "completely drug-free" by December 31, 2029. He also targeted Congress, recalling Rahul Gandhi's 2017 promise that drugs would be eliminated within one term and accusing the party of doing nothing when it was in power.The attack gives the alliance a ready-made campaign plank. But it also puts the BJP and SAD on the spot, as both parties have been part of Punjab's political establishment for decades. The voters, thus, will judge their record as well as their promises.There is another complication. The Congress remains a strong third front and could split the anti-incumbency vote. Rural Sikh voters who continue to view the BJP through the lens of the farm agitation may also be reluctant to back the reunited partners. The AAP could benefit if opposition votes remain divided.The BJP-SAD reunion also complicates the Congress's position. With an established opposition pole, the contest for voters dissatisfied with the AAP government will now intensify. Amit Shah's attack on the Congress over its record on drugs made it clear that the alliance intends to take on both the ruling party and its principal rival.The Congress can still draw on its independent support base, but it will have to navigate a more crowded opposition space, as well as its own internal factional differences.Six years after a split that left both allies on the margins, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have chosen pragmatism over past grievances to challenge AAP and Congress. The 2027 election, however, will not be a simple replay of the coalition's past victories. And tough seat-sharing talks are yet to be held.The OGs may be back together, but winning over a changed Punjab will require more than old chemistry.
Article Summary: BJP and SAD announce revival of alliance for 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first.

Article Title: ‘Sitting at the feet of the same BJP’: Bhagwant Mann attacks Sukhbir Badal over alliance
Article Text:
Bhagwant Mann attacks Sukhbir Badal over alliance

BJP and SAD revive alliance after six-year break

NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Tuesday criticised the newly announced alliance between Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the 2027 Assembly elections, accusing SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of aligning with the same party he had previously criticised over its handling of farmers' issues.In a video statement shared by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Mann alleged that the Badal family had initially supported the three farm laws introduced by the Centre in 2020 but changed its stand after the farmers' protest gained momentum and widespread support.Referring to the resignation of then Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Mann claimed the Akali Dal had realised that it would struggle to survive politically in Punjab if it continued to support the laws."The BJP and the Akali Dal have formed an alliance. I would like to remind you of what they say to each other, how these people try to make a fool of the public. They feel that people forget things after some time. At first, the entire Badal family kept speaking in favour of these 'black laws', saying, 'That's a very good law, a very good law. It is amazing; if it does amazing work, then with this, the agriculture of Punjab will become very prosperous.' When the farmers' movement reached its peak and started getting support from all over the world, they realised this would be a mistake and that it would be difficult to survive politically in Punjab," he said."So, Harsimrat resigned and started speaking against those laws, claiming, 'The BJP is anti-farmer, the BJP is anti-farmer, we have sacrificed, the BJP is anti-farmer.' But by then, people understood that they were still in talks with each other and were separating from each other just to put on a show for the public," he added.Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet in September 2020, before the Lok Sabha voted on the farm bills. Days after the Rajya Sabha cleared the final bill, Sukhbir Singh Badal announced the SAD's unanimous decision to withdraw from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).Mann also accused the BJP of neglecting Punjab's interests, citing the state's tableau at national events on Republic Day and Independence Day."The same BJP says that the tableau that comes out on January 26 or August 15 will not be Punjab's tableau in Delhi. We got this work done by fighting with them," he said.Targeting Sukhbir Badal over his earlier criticism of the BJP, Mann alleged that the SAD president had accused the party of interfering in Sikh religious institutions with the help of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)."The same BJP about which Sukhbir Badal used to say that Sikh organisations are being taken over by the BJP with the help of the RSS, that the BJP has captured the committee of Hazur Sahib in Maharashtra and the committee of Patna Sahib. Today, sitting at the feet of that same BJP, you are making a political alliance," he said.Appealing to people to support the AAP government, Mann said, "Aam Aadmi Party is your own party. There is a party living in your hearts. I will come at your call, wherever you call me. We will come and raise our voice in favour of Punjab."Mann's remarks came after BJP and SAD announced on Tuesday that they would contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections together, reviving their alliance after a six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats, with the SAD taking the lead in the arrangement."Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats. Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," Union Home Minister Amit Shah said at a joint press conference attended by BJP president Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal."Naturally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will play the role of the elder brother. The Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will contest together. Both parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, while the Akali Dal will be in the role of the elder brother," Shah added.The announcement, made on Gurpurab, marked the revival of ties between the two parties, which ended their partnership in 2020 after the SAD withdrew from the NDA over its opposition to the farm laws.Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 Assembly seats, while the SAD fielded candidates in the remaining constituencies. The two parties had jointly governed the state for 10 years before losing the 2017 Assembly elections, when the Congress returned to power under Captain Amarinder Singh.In the 2022 Assembly elections, the AAP swept to power, while the BJP and SAD, which contested separately, were pushed to the margins.Meanwhile, the Punjab BJP on Monday announced its 16-member state election committee for the 2027 Assembly polls, with state president Kewal Singh Dhillon heading the panel.
Article Summary: BJP and SAD revive alliance after six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats, with the SAD taking the lead in the arrangement. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann accused SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of aligning with the same party he had previously criticised over its handling of farmers' issues.

Article Title: Watch: In a jibe on Meta, Abhijeet Dipke praises PM Modi, then calls for Constitution Day rally

NEW DELHI: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a Constitution Day rally in Nagpur on November 26. He urged people to join the event under the slogans of "Save Democracy and Save Constitution".In a video posted on X, he also took a sarcastic dig at Meta, alleging that social media posts glorifying PM Modi receive greater visibility and engagement on its platforms.The video begins with Dipke making remarks about PM Modi, saying, "In front of Modi Ji's radiance, the sun's light also becomes dim. In front of Modi Ji's speech, the sky's speech also becomes dim."He further says, "If there is Modi Ji, then this is a country. If there is Modi Ji, then this is the world. If there is no Modi, then there is nothing."He then reveals the apparent target of his sarcasm, saying, "This was for Meta, now let's talk about work." The remarks appear to be a sarcastic reference to what Dipke alleges is Meta's portrayal of PM Modi through excessive praise.Moving on to the rally announcement, Dipke said the Cockroach Janta Party would organise the event in Nagpur at 4 pm on November 26, coinciding with Constitution Day.Calling on people to participate, he said, "All of you have to come there and together we have to stand up for our country's democracy and constitution."He concluded by reiterating his appeal, saying, "Please be there on 26th November, 4 pm. Thank you."He ends the video with the song "Modi hai toh mumkin hai" playing alongside a photograph of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a Constitution Day rally in Nagpur on November 26. He urged people to join the event under the slogans of "Save Democracy and Save Constitution" In a video posted on X, he also took a sarcastic dig at Meta, alleging that social media posts glorifying PM Modi receive greater visibility and engagement.

Article Title: Karthigai Deepam lit at Tamil Nadu temple, not pillar as ordered by SC; scuffle erupts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A small team of priests of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple lit a lamp on Tuesday, days after the Supreme Court permitted the ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Thiruparankundram hill.The Karthigai Deepam was lit at the traditional site above the Uchhipillaiyar temple and not at the Deepathoon.Meanwhile, police forcibly detained members of Hindu outfits as a scuffle broke out at the entrance to the hill pathway.Members of Hindu outfits stood at the entrance to the pathway and raised slogans against the government.The ceremony was held amid heightened security, with police detaining several people citing apprehensions of disorder based on intelligence inputs and their past conduct.Several BJP leaders and members of Hindu organisations were also detained across Tamil Nadu as police enforced restrictions ahead of the ceremony.Later in the day, the Madras high court's Madurai Bench, however, directed the Tamil Nadu government and all authorities concerned to comply with the Supreme Court's November 20 order permitting the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.It also directed officials to release all persons unlawfully detained under prohibitory orders imposed in Thiruparankundram.The direction was issued to the district collector, police commissioner and temple authorities amid restrictions surrounding the ceremony.The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The Subramaniya Swamy Temple is situated at the foothills, while a Dargah is located near the hilltop. A Shiva temple is also situated on the hill.Hindu groups maintain that the stone pillar where they seek to light the lamp belongs to the temple, citing civil court decisions dating back about a century.Dargah officials and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute involves questions of ownership and the rights of the respective parties.On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah.The apex court specified that the ceremony must be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.
Article Summary: The Karthigai Deepam was lit at the traditional site above the Uchhipillaiyar temple and not at the Deepathoon. Police forcibly detained members of Hindu outfits as a scuffle broke out at the entrance to the hill pathway. The Madras high court's Madurai Bench directed the Tamil Nadu government and all authorities concerned to comply with the Supreme Court order.

Article Title: 'Comply with SC order, release detainees': Madras HC directs Tamil Nadu government ahead of deepam lighting

NEW DELHI: The Madras HC's Madurai Bench on Tuesday directed the Tamil Nadu government and all authorities concerned to comply with the Supreme Court 's order permitting the ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Thiruparankundram hill. It also directed the officials to release all persons unlawfully detained under Thiruparankundram prohibitory orders.The direction was issued to the district collector, police commissioner and temple authorities amid heightened security and restrictions ahead of the ceremony.The court's intervention came amid a dispute over the implementation of the apex court's November 20 order, which permitted a one-time lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.The state informed the HC that 258 persons have detained apprehending disorder based on intelligence and past conduct.Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran, who was placed under house arrest while attempting to visit Thiruparankundram, accused the police of preventing him from exercising his fundamental rights."In the absence of any legally valid prohibitory order, the police are preventing me from visiting the temple to offer prayers. Preventing us from leaving our homes in the name of arrest amounts to a violation of an individual's fundamental rights," he said.Citing Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution, Nagenthran said citizens had the right to worship according to their faith and freely practise religious activities."However, these fundamental rights are being denied in Tamil Nadu. Despite the Supreme Court's directions, how can restrictions on lighting the ceremonial lamp and offering prayers at sacred places such as Thiruparankundram be justified?" he said.He also alleged that around 200 police personnel had been deployed outside his residence since morning and that police vehicles followed him even when he attempted to drop his children at school."Such acts of oppression are taking place only in Tamil Nadu and are not witnessed in any other state," he said.Nagenthran further accused the state government of using the restrictions to divert public attention from other issues, including sexual harassment allegations against ruling party members and MLAs and the Kallakurichi incident.The dispute centres on a demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The issue has been contested for more than three decades through representations to temple authorities, government-facilitated peace meetings and legal proceedings.The Supreme Court, in its November 20 interim order, permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah. It directed that the ceremony be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.The Tamil Nadu government moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its interim order.The Madurai district administration had imposed prohibitory orders from November 23 night until November 25 morning, banning public gatherings, rallies and unauthorised climbing of the hill. Security was also tightened, with more than 5,600 police personnel deployed across the hill and surrounding areas.
Article Summary: Madras HC directs Tamil Nadu officials to follow the Supreme Court's Deepam lighting order amid heightened tensions. Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran, who was placed under house arrest while attempting to visit Thiruparankundram, accused police of preventing him from exercising his fundamental rights.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday said his party was willing to make adjustments and accommodations to secure an alliance with the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, as seat-sharing discussions between the two INDIA bloc partners continued for the second consecutive day in New Delhi.Akhilesh said senior leaders from both parties were engaged in negotiations aimed at ensuring electoral victory, but refrained from disclosing details of the proposed seat-sharing arrangement, saying several aspects were still under consideration."Regarding the ongoing discussions, our party's senior leaders, along with those entrusted by the party to handle these talks, are currently engaged in the process. What exactly is being discussed? How many seats are being agreed upon, and how many could the other party potentially win? These matters are under consideration, so it is difficult to say anything definitive right now. Alliances are formed with the sole objective of winning; the purpose of an alliance is victory," he said.Emphasising the need for a united effort against the BJP, Yadav said the SP was prepared to make compromises given the electoral challenge ahead."The Samajwadi Party is committed to making adjustments and accommodations because the battle ahead is significant. The goal is to win, and we must win, especially against a political 'machine' like the BJP, we have to prepare accordingly and make the right decisions," he added.Akhilesh also questioned the functioning of constitutional bodies and the Election Commission of India (ECI), alleging that concerns were being raised over the possible addition of votes and the maintenance of electronic voting machines (EVMs)."Constitutional bodies have a duty to act fairly, yet questions are being raised about this very body. It is now being suggested that the BJP is planning to add approximately 3 crore votes. Furthermore, regarding the warehouses where EVMs are stored, who are the engineers tasked by the ECI with maintaining these machines? We are told that the machines are being 'serviced,' but no one knows who these engineers actually are," he said.After Tuesday's meeting, SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said the discussions had covered individual constituencies and described the negotiations as positive."Look, we have discussed every seat individually, and the discussions have been very positive. However, 403 seats are a very large number, aren't they? So, the discussions have not yet been completed. But you can rest assured that we will finalise everything in the next two meetings," he said.Ahead of the meeting, Ram Gopal Yadav had confirmed that the SP proposed allocating 26 seats to the Congress, including two constituencies won by the party in the 2022 Assembly elections, four where it finished second and 20 where the SP secured between 60,000 and 70,000 votes, while the Congress received around 2,000 votes."We have proposed offering two seats that the Congress won in the 2022 Assembly elections. Additionally, there are four seats where the Congress finished in second place, and 20 other seats where the SP secured between 60,000 and 70,000 votes, while the Congress received only about 2,000 votes," he told reporters.The Congress had submitted a list of 130 priority constituencies to the SP leadership during the first round of discussions on Monday. SP leaders agreed to examine the list and continue negotiations.Both parties agreed to contest the Assembly elections together and indicated that the seat-sharing arrangement could be finalised within the next two to four days.Describing Monday's meeting as cordial, Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said the discussions lasted around 20 minutes, with both sides approaching the negotiations positively."We took just about 20 minutes to wrap up day one of the talks in which we discussed the number of seats (with SP). The SP panel members heard us and said they would get back after talking to their party chief Akhilesh Yadav ji," Gautam told PTI.He said both parties were committed to contesting together and would reach a mutually acceptable seat-sharing arrangement. Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee president Aradhana Misra-Mona also indicated that an agreement was likely within the next two to four days.Tuesday's meeting was held at the residence of senior Congress leader Pramod Tiwari. The Congress delegation included Gautam, Misra-Mona, working president Imran Masood and Congress Legislative Party leader Virendra Chaudhary.The SP delegation comprised Ram Gopal Yadav, state president Shyam Lal Pal, MP Rajiv Rai, Awadhesh Prasad and MP Iqra Hasan.Meanwhile, SP leader Azam Khan said no one could stop him from contesting an election, expressing confidence in the party's election symbol."Who can stop me from contesting an election? My bicycle will contest the election; the bicycle will win... Samajwadis' focus is very narrow. They see nothing beyond the bicycle. These people don't even think about cars, helicopters, or airplanes..." he said.BJP leader and former Union minister Sanjeev Balyan said his party would seek to counter the electoral perception created by the SP and Congress during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and return to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term."We are making efforts to ensure that the perception created during the 2024 elections does not succeed this time. We will take these issues (development and law and order) before the people. The BJP will form the government again," Balyan told PTI Videos during an interview in Muzaffarnagar.The former Muzaffarnagar MP also dismissed the Congress's electoral prospects in the state, saying the party did not have a significant support base in Uttar Pradesh.On the SP's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) outreach, Balyan questioned the changing definition of the acronym used by Akhilesh Yadav."Let Akhilesh Yadav first give a final definition of PDA, then we can respond. Sometimes one group is included in it, sometimes another. If there was any PDA during his government, it was limited to a particular section of the backward communities," he alleged.Balyan further claimed that the SP government had failed to ensure adequate representation for different backward communities and Dalits, despite the party's current emphasis on social justice and representation.Asked whether the SP-Congress alliance's strategy, including its outreach through panchayats, had contributed to the BJP's defeat in several western Uttar Pradesh constituencies in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Balyan said electoral outcomes could not be attributed to a single factor.The 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly is scheduled to go to polls in February-March next year. The BJP has been in power in the state since 2017, winning two consecutive Assembly elections.The SP and Congress contested the 2022 Assembly elections separately. However, the two parties joined hands as INDIA bloc partners for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and jointly won 43 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 parliamentary seats.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav says his party is willing to make adjustments and accommodations to secure an alliance with the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Yadav refrained from disclosing details of the proposed seat-sharing arrangement, saying several aspects were still under consideration.

NEW DELHI: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar's grandnephew has sent a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi , demanding an unconditional apology and correction over remarks about the freedom fighter in her memoir, alleging a "distorted portrayal" of his ancestor.Satyaki Savarkar, the paternal grandnephew of VD Savarkar, has objected to statements on pages 201 and 443 of the book,alleging that they are factually inaccurate, historically misleading and prejudicial to Savarkar's reputation and legacy, PTI reported.The notice, issued by advocate Sangram Kolhatkar on Satyaki Savarkar's behalf, asks Sonia Gandhi to meet the demands within 15 days of receiving it.It warns that failure to comply could prompt legal proceedings before a competent court or authority.The notice refers to a statement on page 201 of the memoir, which reads, "While Congress freedom fighters were enduring assaults and imprisonment at the hands of the British rulers, senior ideologues of the RSS like Vinayak Damodar Savarkar were writing mercy petitions to their colonial masters, and their members were colluding with the British authorities as informers."Satyaki Savarkar alleges that the statement creates an impression that VD Savarkar was involved in informing on or collaborating with the British authorities against Indian freedom fighters.The notice disputes this implication, saying it is unsupported by the historical context of Savarkar's imprisonment, petitions and political activities.It states that Savarkar endured prolonged imprisonment and severe hardships under British rule, including incarceration in the Cellular Jail in the Andaman Islands.It further argues that references to his petitions without examining the circumstances and historical background present an incomplete and distorted account of his life and political struggle.The notice also objects to a statement on page 443, which reads, "A contrary vision, articulated by Gandhiji's contemporary Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, the founder of the ideology known as Hindutva, views India as primarily a nation where Hindus are supreme-an outlook espoused by the RSS, the BJP, and their numerous affiliates across the country known collectively as the 'Sangh Parivar,' or 'Family of the RSS'."It alleges that the passage oversimplifies and misrepresents Savarkar's political and ideological philosophy, arguing that his writings, speeches and views need to be considered in their proper historical, intellectual and political context.According to the notice, the two statements, when read together, present a distorted account of Savarkar's role in the freedom struggle and his political philosophy, potentially misleading readers and creating an unjustified adverse impression of his legacy.The legal notice also refers to actions taken by the government during former prime minister Indira Gandhi's tenure and her personal contributions, which it says recognised Savarkar's stature as a patriot and freedom fighter.It cites the issuance of a commemorative postage stamp in Savarkar's honour, as well as Indira Gandhi's personal contribution of Rs 11,000 from her bank account towards the Swatantryaveer Savarkar Rashtriya Smarak.It argues that these official acts and Indira Gandhi's personal contribution demonstrate recognition of Savarkar's patriotism and asks Sonia Gandhi to explain how the statements in her memoir can be reconciled with these records.The notice calls on Sonia Gandhi to substantiate the statements with authentic historical material or acknowledge "inaccuracies and misleading implications" and take corrective measures.It seeks a written, unequivocal and unconditional apology for the statements, along with a public clarification explaining their historical basis, context and intended meaning and acknowledging and correcting any factual inaccuracies or misleading implications.It also asks Sonia Gandhi to take appropriate steps, in consultation with HarperCollins Publishers India, to "correct, suitably qualify or withdraw the objectionable statements from subsequent editions, reprints and electronic versions of the publication".The notice states that the memoir, authored by Sonia Gandhi and published by HarperCollins Publishers India, was reportedly released on November 10.Satyaki Savarkar said he recently came across the book and was disturbed by the statements and imputations concerning VD Savarkar.
Article Summary: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar's grandnephew has sent a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi. He is demanding an unconditional apology and correction over remarks about the freedom fighter in her memoir. The notice alleges a "distorted portrayal" of his ancestor.

NEW DELHI: Chemical contaminants detected in a batch of packaged drinking water manufactured by Bisleri at its Goa facility has raised concerns over potential health risks, including kidney damage and cancer.Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) reportedly declared the sample unsafe after tests flagged bromate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Bisleri, however, has disputed the findings, maintaining that its water is safe for consumption.Dr Tanmay Pandya, HoD and director, Nephrology and Renal Transplantation, Sarvodaya Hospital, Faridabad, said prolonged exposure to certain chemical contaminants could affect kidney function, depending on their concentration and duration of exposure. "Bromate is a chemical of concern because of its potential carcinogenic properties," he said, adding that certain heavy metals and industrial chemicals could also interfere with kidney function.In a statement issued Monday, Bisleri said FSSAI collected six samples from its Goa manufacturing facility on Sept 30, 2025.While five met the applicable standards, the sixth recorded bromate at 12 micrograms per litre against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre, the company said in a statement.Following an appeal, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory in Nov 2025. Bisleri said the laboratory found bromate within the prescribed limit but separately flagged PAHs. The company subsequently got the sample tested at an FSSAI-approved independent laboratory, which also found bromate within the prescribed limit.Bisleri said it submitted the independent laboratory results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office on Feb 2, 2026, but received no further communication. It also claimed it had not received the reported notice by email or in hard copy.The company said it follows a 10-stage purification process, conducts over 90 quality tests and will cooperate with FSSAI.Explaining the contamination concerns, Dr Saurabh Arora, MD of Auriga Research, said packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are regulated under separate standards. Bromate can form during water treatment, while PAHs may enter through packaging or contamination during bottling.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) reportedly declared the sample unsafe. Tests flagged bromate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) Bisleri has disputed the findings, maintaining that its water is safe for consumption.

Article Title: Bangladeshi court orders interim curbs on social media access for children under 16
Article Text:
The court issued the directives Sunday while passing an order on a writ petition

DHAKA: Bangladeshi court has directed the authorities to frame mandatory interim guidelines to prevent children below 16 years of age from accessing social media platforms and ordered the formation of an independent expert committee to examine the impact of algorithm-driven content feeds on minors.The High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh issued the directives on Sunday while passing an order on a writ petition that questioned the government's failure to formulate a national policy regulating social media access for children under 16, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.The bench comprising Justices Sikder Mahmudur Razi and Fatema Anwar directed the Secretary of the Posts and Telecommunications Division and the Chairman of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission, among other respondents, to take necessary steps.It also ordered the immediate formation of a committee comprising cybersecurity specialists, child psychologists, paediatricians and legal experts to assess the structural impact of algorithm-controlled feeds on children.The move comes amid growing international concerns over the impact of social media on children's mental health, physical well-being and development, with governments across the globe increasingly considering age-based restrictions and stricter safeguards against potentially harmful online content.The committee will examine how algorithm-based recommendation systems influence children's behaviour, exposure to online content and overall development, and submit its assessment to help shape regulatory measures.The writ petition was filed earlier this month by Supreme Court lawyer Mohammad Faisal Dastagir, who appeared before the court in person.The absence of a regulatory framework had left children below 16 exposed to unrestricted social media use, potentially affecting their mental and physical development, Dastagir was quoted as saying by Prothom Alo.Citing research highlighting health concerns, including impaired eyesight, among children exposed to excessive screen time, he argued that a national policy was necessary to regulate their access to social media.The court also directed the authorities to explain why their failure to establish an independent committee to assess the structural impact of algorithm-controlled feeds on minors and formulate a national policy restricting social media access for children under 16 should not be declared illegal and beyond their lawful authority, the report said.Several countries across the world are tightening regulations governing children's access to social media.Australia became the first country to enforce a minimum age of 16 for accounts on major social media platforms in December 2025, requiring platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent under-16s from creating or retaining accounts.Indonesia banned children under 16 from having accounts on "high-risk" social media and online platforms starting on March 28, 2026, making it the first country in Southeast Asia to introduce such restrictions.Malaysia, too, began enforcing age-verification requirements in June 2026, barring children below 16 from opening social media accounts and requiring existing users to verify their age.The UK plans to ban children under 16 from major social media platforms starting in spring 2027, with initial regulations expected to be laid before Parliament by December 2026. It is also considering overnight curfews for teens aged 16 and 17 and blocking infinite-scroll mechanisms for kids.Canada introduced a bill in parliament in June, proposing a minimum age of 16 for holding social media accounts. The proposed legislation is yet to become law.Brazil enacted rules in 2026 requiring age verification and parental account linking for users under 16.The European Commission has proposed the EU KIDS Act in September to ban children under 13 from social media and set 15 as the minimum age for independent accounts.Countries such as France, Greece, Turkey, Spain, Poland, New Zealand, Denmark, and Slovenia have drafted restrictions aimed primarily at under-15s, while Austria has proposed an under-14 ban.
Article Summary: The High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh issued the directives on Sunday. The move comes amid growing international concerns over the impact of social media on children's mental health, physical well-being and development. Several countries across the world are tightening regulations governing children's access to social media.

Article Title: China’s mega dam takes shape near Arunachal Pradesh: Satellite data
Article Text:
India has proposed 11,200MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project to cushion the impactof sudden changes in water discharge from China

GUWAHATI: Fresh satellite imagery analysis by an Indian geospatial AI deep tech start-up incubated at FITT, IIT Delhi, shows construction of China’s 60 GW Medog hydropower project on Yarlung Tsangpo (the Siang in India) is advanced and widespread.According to the findings of the public-release assessment by EarthSense Labs, entire villages had been cleared at the main dam site, river diversion works were visible and heavy industrial infrastructure had been built near the Arunachal Pradesh border.The findings are significant for India as it has proposed the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh. Project proponents say SUMP is intended to cushion the downstream impact of the Chinese project.The Chinese project is close to the McMahon Line , about 40 km to 50 km north of Arunachal Pradesh.The EarthSense report places the tunnel exit near the border, downstream of Medog County. The SUMP, proposed on Siang river, would be located further downstream in India, across Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts. Its proposed reservoir is expected by project proponents to hold nine billion cubic metres of water.The Chinese project will be a multi-structure dam system along the lower Yarlung Tsangpo river in southeastern Tibet.It will include a tunnel across the river’s famous “Great U-Bend”, multiple power stations and outlets before the river enters India, the report said.The report lists four critical locations and assets — a large dam near Mainling town, where “work has started extensively after July 2025”; a lower dam, possibly near Pai town; a tunnel through Namcha Barwa Mountain; and a tunnel outlet near the India-China border, downstream of Medog County, where work has also started.“Developmental work on the tunnel outlet area has started even before the ground-breaking ceremony,” the report said.The project is planned as five cascade stations at an estimated cost of 1.2 trillion yuan (roughly $168 billion). It would use tunnels of around 40 km to exploit a river drop of more than 2,000 metres over a stretch of about 50 km, the report said.EarthSense Labs’ study of imagery from July 2025 showed villages and farm fields at the site of the proposed Mainling high dam. By Dec 2025, the villages were cleared, the fields removed and earthwork had begun, it said.Imagery of Aug 2026 showed diversion works, the relocation of entire villages and the emergence of new roads, makeshift housing and office buildings on the north bank.The key finding, according to the report, was “Site clearance and earthwork after July 2025, followed by river diversion works by Aug 2026.”Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu has pointed out that the proposed SUMP reservoir, with a storage capacity of about 9.2 billion cubic metres (BCM), is expected to give India greater control over downstream flows. Khandu had said the Siang reservoir, with a capacity greater than the reported 5.2 BCM of China’s project, would help regulate river flows, respond to sudden changes in upstream discharge and maintain water availability during lean seasons. Khandu has repeatedly flagged the absence of a binding water-sharing treaty and transparent data-sharing arrangement with China as a major vulnerability.Opposition to SUMP has hardened on the ground. Adi communities have petitioned Union home minister Amit Shah , citing concerns over displacement, land and livelihoods. Central armed police forces were deployed near the proposed site as tensions rose over a pre-feasibility survey. In Oct, violence broke out during protests.The report documents the scale and pace of construction but does not quantify environmental damage, downstream flow effects or risks to Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. Its locations are described as indicative, and the analysis relies on satellite imagery.A video featuring Adi environmental engineer Katon Moyong criticising the proposed 11,200MW Siang dam disappeared from public view in India after Meta restricted access following a govt notice, according to a notification displayed on the Facebook post of a digital news outlet in the state that had uploaded the clip.The video, posted by Arunachal Today on Nov 21, showed Moyong — aka Abor Man — explaining his opposition to the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project during home minister Amit Shah’s visit to the state. The post now displays the message: “Video not available in India.”In a notification dated Nov 22, Meta said it had restricted the content “pursuant to a notice from Govt of India under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, 2000”. The notice warned that sharing similar content could lead to further restrictions on the outlet’s account in India.Arunachal Today said the notification did not disclose the specific grounds or details of the govt notice. It also raised questions over the curbs on social media content concerning the contentious Siang dam debate.
Article Summary: Satellite imagery analysis by an Indian geospatial AI deep tech start-up incubated at FITT, IIT Delhi, shows construction of China’s 60 GW Medog hydropower project on Yarlung Tsangpo (the Siang in India) is advanced and widespread. The findings are significant for India as it has proposed the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh. Project proponents say SUMP is intended to cushion the downstream impact of the Chinese project.

Article Title: Don't be a Baahubali: SC to Bihar judge over criminal case against SP
Article Text:
SC flags the judge's behaviour, says every judge must knowcontours of his jurisdiction

Pitiable plight

NEW DELHI: An additional sessions judge in Bihar's Sasaram was chastised on Monday by Supreme Court which took exception to him flexing his position and getting a criminal case registered against a superintendent of police who did not carry out his order, and asked the judge "not to be Quixotic or play Robin Hood or Baahubali of Bihar".The ASJ, in a criminal trial, had directed the SP to file an FIR against a witness for deposing falsely. After his repeated summons were not complied with, the judge directed the Bihar chief secretary to take disciplinary action against the SP.When that did not work, the ASJ directed a criminal case against the SP and asked him to appear in court Aug 22. After two adjournments, the SP's counsel sought permission for virtual appearance on the grounds that he was supervising flood relief.In the meantime, the inspecting judge from the HC asked the sessions judge to meet him with the case records in Patna on Sept 24, which the judicial officer declined saying "it was very humiliating and demoralising" for him. On Sept 29, the sessions judge convicted the SP for flouting court orders and fined him Re 1.On the state govt's appeal, Patna HC criticised the judicial officer's conduct and asked him to be circumspect and exercise caution in future.Hurt by these remarks, the judicial officer appealed against the HC judgment before the SC and said, "The present case depicts the pitiable plight of judicial officers once they pass any order against an IAS or IPS officer. The entire system tends to protect them, leaving judicial officers high and dry. "A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said every judge was bound by procedure and asked if a district judge could behave like this? "When an inspecting judge asks you to meet him, why would you not go?" the bench asked."Every judge must know the contours of his jurisdiction. Don't be Quixotic or a Robin Hood," the bench said and asked the judicial officer's counsel Prem Prakash to convey to him not "to become Baahubali of Bihar".The bench said in its order, "Regardless of the observations made by the HC in its Oct 8 order, we request the HC to consider petitioner judicial officer's explanation-cum-apology sympathetically and dispose of the pending proceedings."On another judicial officer's petition complaining about promotion and selection to higher judicial service, the CJI-led bench said, "It has become a fashion for judicial officers to rush to the SC directly without approaching the HCs concerned. They are thinking 24x7 about promotion, increase in salary and perks and extension of retirement age, paying little attention to deal with huge pendency."
Article Summary: An additional sessions judge in Bihar's Sasaram was chastised on Monday by Supreme Court. He got a criminal case registered against a superintendent of police who did not carry out his order. The ASJ, in a criminal trial, had directed the SP to file an FIR against a witness for deposing falsely.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said priority must be given to the appeals of 22 lakh people, of the total 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll, and sought the state govt's response to allegations that voters deleted during SIR are being denied ration and benefits under various social welfare schemes.The court also said even among the 22 lakh, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation should be heard ahead of others, keeping in view the upcoming civic elections.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the Calcutta HC chief justice in consultation with Election Commission must increase the number of tribunals - currently 19 - to deal with the 38 lakh appeals, filed on deletion of 90 lakh voters declared absent, shifted, duplicate or dead, or flagged for 'logical discrepancy', related to mapping.The bench also asked Election Commission to requisition additional space for housing the tribunals at various places to facilitate easy access to appellants.SC's direction came after advocate Prashant Bhushan told SC that of the 1.4 lakh appeals decided so far by tribunals, which were appointed to adjudicate a large number of appeals filed after SIR, more than 90% have been allowed leading to restoration of their names in the electoral roll.This is a strong indicator based on a large sample size to persuade the top court to direct that those who have filed appeals against deletion of their names should be allowed to vote in the coming elections, Bhushan said.Supreme Court said this was the reason for it to ask for prioritisation of appeals for restoration of names relating to various wards in KMC.Bhushan, supported by senior advocate G Sankaranarayanan, told the apex court that even though the court had categorically clarified that deletion of names from electoral roll would not have any consequence, including with regard to citizenship, beyond the chance to vote, state govt has been denying the deleted voters ration through public distribution system (PDS) and benefits under social welfare schemes, including Annapurna Yojna.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said these are bald assertions and alleged that the petitioners have not cited a single example to substantiate their claims.However, the CJI-led bench asked state govt to file response to the allegations.In a related issue, SC postponed to Wednesday hearing on state govt's appeal challenging an interim order of a division bench of Calcutta HC restraining the state EC from announcing schedule for KMC polls, in which the number of wards were increased from 144 to 209 by an amending Act. Mehta said the high court mistakenly concluded that state govt lacked the jurisdiction to carry out the exercise of increasing the number of wards and resultant adjustment of ward boundaries.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said priority must be given to the appeals of 22 lakh people, of the total 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll. The court also said even among the 22 lakh, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation should be heard ahead of others.

After participating in the SCO inaugural civilisational dialogue in New Delhi, Pakistan is now all set to deliver an invitation to India for a meeting of the culture ministers it will host under its presidency of the Eurasian bloc early next year. It will be interesting to see how India responds as no Indian minister has visited Pakistan since the Pahalgam terrorist attack.Significantly, Islamabad is also preparing to host the SCO heads of state council summit - where India is usually represented by PM Narendra Modi -next year in late August, after initially considering having it on August 14 – Pakistan's Independence Day. An August 14 summit is unlikely to have seen participation by India at any level.The only significant visit to Pakistan from India after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack was by MEA additional secretary Alok Dimri for a meeting of the SCO national coordinators in September – shortly after Pakistan assumed presidency – to firm up the calendar of events under Islamabad's stewardship.After what is officially called Meeting of Ministers of Culture (SCO-MMC), Pakistan will also host more high-profile meetings of the SCO defence and foreign ministers in the run up to the Islamabad summit in August.The meeting for cultural cooperation among SCO member-states in Pakistan is a relatively low-stakes event for India that keeps political commitments minimal, unlike the foreign and defence high-level gatherings which might raise the political temperature at home.The last minister to visit Pakistan was S Jaishankar for a meeting of the SCO foreign ministers' meeting in October 2024, well before Pahalgam.Amid criticism by the Opposition for hosting Pakistan minister Musadik Malik for the Modi-proposed civilisational dialogue last week, India reiterated there was no dilution of its position on the Indus Waters Treaty that was "put in abeyance" after the Pahalgam attack. India has stressed that SCO cooperation should not be mistaken for bilateral thaw.The visit by Malik passed off smoothly without any bilateral friction as he adhered to the protocol of addressing multilateral SCO themes, rather than raising sensitive bilateral issues.While the key question remains whether Modi will travel to Islamabad for the SCO summit, Indian officials say such a visit is highly improbable at this stage. Any bilateral thaw that might result in Modi's visit requires, as far as India is concerned, a fundamental shift in Pakistan's position on cross-border terrorism.India is seeking tangible progress on its security concerns and doesn't want to create any optics of normalisation when these concerns remain unaddressed.The possibility of a senior minister, most likely Jaishankar, representing India is not ruled out. It would allow India to sustain its active engagement with the SCO, while not being seen as softening its Pakistan policy. Officials point to the fact that there's already a precedent for that. In 2024, it was Jaishankar who attended the heads of summit in Kazakhstan, filling in for the PM.
Article Summary: Pakistan is set to deliver an invitation to India for a meeting of the culture ministers it will host under its presidency of the Eurasian bloc early next year. No Indian minister has visited Pakistan since the Pahalgam terrorist attack. Islamabad is also preparing to host the SCO heads of state council summit next year in late August.

NEW DELHI: The 1977 election defeat followed the Gandhi family into childhood, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi recalled, sharing memories of school taunts and tense days at home in a candid conversation with their mother Sonia Gandhi , released in a video on Tuesday.In the video titled ‘What Ma Left Out of Her Book’, the siblings looked back at the days after their grandmother Indira Gandhi and uncle Sanjay lost the election following the Emergency, when the family moved to a different house and, as Priyanka put it, “there was a lot of tension in the air”.The conversation turned to their first day back at school after the electoral defeat. Priyanka recalled a boy approaching her with a taunt about Sanjay, who had been jailed in connection with the ‘Kissa Kursi Ka’ case.“I remember a little boy coming and telling me, ‘Tera chacha jail mein hai; chor hai tera chacha’,” she said. “So I gave him a slap and he started crying. We went to the teacher and I got a scolding.”The siblings’ recollections offered a glimpse of how the political upheaval of the Emergency years spilled into the everyday lives of Indira Gandhi’s grandchildren.Rahul, meanwhile, remembered a different kind of isolation at school.He said that when he sat down on the first day after the election, no one took the seat next to him. He did not say anything, but recalled that classmates were not talking to him and were being “a bit mean”.Sonia Gandhi interjected as Rahul spoke about the remarks children had made about their grandmother. The family also recalled a birthday party that Priyanka had arranged in an attempt to mend things. She had invited 32 children, but 15 minutes after the scheduled time, nobody had arrived. Eventually, only one friend turned up — a friend Rahul said he still has.The conversation also brought out the contrasting personalities of the two siblings. Priyanka said she had been a prefect and was suited to the school system, while Rahul described himself as rebellious, always asking questions and disturbing things.“She wasn’t rebellious. She always followed the rules,” Rahul said of Priyanka. “And I was rebellious, always asking questions.”Priyanka joked that the same difference could be seen in Parliament today, saying she was suited to the system while Rahul was not.The memories come days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which recounts episodes from her family life and the Emergency period.The 1977 election was the only electoral defeat for Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi. It followed the Emergency, imposed from June 1975 to March 1977, during which civil liberties were curtailed and political opponents were jailed.Sanjay Gandhi was convicted in the ‘Kissa Kursi Ka’ case in February 1979, along with former information and broadcasting minister V C Shukla, over charges related to the destruction of prints of the satirical film. The conviction was later overturned on appeal.Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi returned to electoral victory in 1980. Sanjay died in an air crash in 1981, after which Rajiv Gandhi entered politics and won the Amethi seat. He held it until his assassination during the 1991 election campaign.
Article Summary: The 1977 election defeat followed the Gandhi family into childhood, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi recalled. They shared memories of school taunts and tense days at home in a candid conversation with their mother Sonia Gandhi. The 1977 election was the only electoral defeat for Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party BJP ) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday sounded the poll bugle in Punjab, announcing an alliance for the 2027 assembly elections and reviving their partnership after a six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, with the Akali Dal taking the lead in the alliance."Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats.(The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," Union home minister Amit Shah said at a joint press conference attended by BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal."Naturally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will play the role of the elder brother. The Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will contest together. This is our topmost priority, and it will be the foremost issue in the manifestos of both parties," he added.Shah further stated that a detailed manifesto would be finalised soon by the two parties for the elections, but eradicating the drug menace from Punjab and promoting Hindu-Sikh unity would be among the key focus areas."BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free," he added.Delhi minister and BJP leader Manjinder Singh Sirsa said Sukhbir Singh Badal would be the chief ministerial face of the BJP-SAD alliance in Punjab.Speaking to ANI, Sirsa said the alliance was formed with a broader vision of addressing Punjab's problems rather than merely capturing political power. He said its priorities included making the state free of drugs, gangsters and debt, besides resolving farmers' issues.He also congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Shah, Nitin Nabin and Badal on the alliance, and welcomed the SAD's return to NDA.The announcement, made on Gurpurab, comes with a symbolic connection to the events that led to the breakdown of the alliance.The alliance marks a revival of ties between the BJP and SAD, which parted ways in 2020 after the Akali Dal withdrew from the NDA over its opposition to the now-repealed farm laws.Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats, while the SAD fought the remaining constituencies.The two parties had jointly governed Punjab for 10 years before losing the 2017 assembly elections. Congress returned to power under Captain Amarinder Singh.In 2022, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) swept the state, while the BJP and SAD, which contested separately, were pushed to the margins.Meanwhile, the Punjab BJP on Monday announced its 16-member state election committee for the 2027 assembly elections, with state president Kewal Singh Dhillon heading the panel.The committee comprises senior party leaders and former state presidents and has been tasked with preparing the party's electoral roadmap and framing a comprehensive chargesheet against the incumbent government.
Article Summary: The two parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, with the Akali Dal taking the lead in the alliance. Union home minister Amit Shah said tackling drugs, corruption and law and order would be the alliance's key priorities in Punjab. Sukhbir Singh Badal will be the chief ministerial face of the BJP-SAD alliance.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran was placed under house arrest on Tuesday while he was on his way to Thirupparankundram for the Karthigai Deepam festival, amid heightened security over the proposed lighting of a lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.Several BJP leaders and members of Hindu organisations were also detained across the state as police enforced restrictions ahead of the ceremony permitted by the Supreme Court.Condemning the police action, Nagenthran questioned the deployment of a large security force and the detention of party workers and Hindu groups."Deploying over 10,000 policemen is unnecessary, many Hindus, BJP cadres kept under house arrest, we condemn it," he said.Nagenthran planned to visit Thirupparankundram to check whether the lamp would be lit in accordance with the Supreme Court's order. Police personnel were deployed outside his residence in Tirunelveli, news agency PTI reported citing party sources.The BJP said scores of its leaders and cadres, along with members of the Hindu Munnani organisation, were detained to prevent them from travelling to Madurai and checking whether the SC directive was being implemented.In Sivaganga, several Hindu Munnani leaders and members were detained. Police also detained right-wing activists in other parts of Tamil Nadu.The Madurai district administration imposed prohibitory orders from 9pm on November 23 until 10am on November 25, banning public gatherings, rallies and unauthorised climbing of Thirupparankundram hill. However, customary worship, routine temple rituals, lawful access to the dargah and activities implementing Supreme Court directions were exempted.Around 5,618 police personnel, including 12 SPs, eight ASPs and 132 inspectors, were deployed across the hill, temple steps, Girivalam path and surrounding areas.The police also barricaded the Deepathoon and deployed personnel to guard the structure. More than 70 CCTV and facial-recognition cameras were installed, while drone operations were prohibited in the area for two days.The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thirupparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The demand has been pursued for more than three decades through representations to temple authorities, government-facilitated peace meetings and legal proceedings.The Subramanya Swamy temple is situated at the foothills, while a Dargah is located near the hilltop. A Shiva temple is also situated on the hill. Hindu groups maintain that the stone pillar where they seek to light the lamp belongs to the temple, citing civil court decisions dating back about a century.Dargah officials and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute involves questions of ownership and the rights of the respective parties.On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah.The apex court specified that the ceremony must be carried out by an authorised team. It barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.Meanwhile, the Madras HC's Madurai Bench, led by Justice G R Swaminathan, summoned officials amid the restrictions imposed by the district administration.
Article Summary: Several leaders detained, security tightened at Thirupparankundram hill. The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon. The demand has been pursued for more than three decades through representations to temple authorities, government- facilitated peace meetings and legal proceedings.

Article Title: 'NDA is now complete': BJP welcomes back 'oldest ally' Akali Dal ahead of Punjab polls
Article Text:
BJP welcomes back 'oldest ally' Akali Dal ahead of Punjab polls
